result.summary: Optimizes BIP352 silent payment input key extraction for P2SH inputs by checking the witness stack before evaluating the scriptSig. Because only P2SH-P2WPKH inputs are eligible and consensus requires non-segwit P2SH inputs to have an empty witness, inputs without a compressed witness public key are rejected immediately.
result.problem: When scanning transactions for silent payment eligibility, verifying whether a P2SH input is P2SH-P2WPKH evaluates the scriptSig before checking for a witness. Non-segwit P2SH inputs can carry scriptSigs up to 10,000 bytes, causing unnecessary script evaluation overhead during block or transaction scanning.
evidence: Commit message and PR description: "Consensus forbids a witness on non-segwit P2SH inputs, so check the witness (and the cheap pubkey size check) before evaluating the scriptSig. This avoids evaluating scriptSigs of up to MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE for the common case of non-segwit P2SH spends."
result.card: Skips scriptSig evaluation for non-segwit P2SH inputs during BIP352 silent payment input parsing. Under BIP352, only P2SH-P2WPKH inputs are eligible, which require a witness, whereas consensus mandates an empty witness for legacy P2SH spends. By checking the witness stack and public key size before executing script evaluation, the scanner avoids parsing scriptSigs of up to 10,000 bytes on legacy P2SH transactions. A bug here could cause silent payment wallets to miss eligible inputs and fail to detect incoming funds.

risk.why: Incorrectly rejecting eligible inputs during BIP352 key extraction would cause silent payment wallets to compute incorrect shared secrets and miss incoming transactions.
